card.title: Agar data ka ek hissa chhupa dein aur result sahi nikle, to wo science hai?
card.hook: Millikan ka oil-drop experiment sabse famous measurement hai. Par notebooks khuli to pata chala 1913 ke paper mein unhone observations ka ek hissa hi chhapa tha.

detail.real_life_scene: 1913 ke paper mein Millikan ne apne observations ka ek hissa hi publish kiya. Baad mein notebooks ka study hua to pata chala chhoda gaya data 'galat' nahi tha — sirf result se utni achhi tarah match nahi karta tha.
detail.central_question: Kya Millikan ne experiment ke sirf favourable results publish kiye?

explanation.heading: Problem: charge ki basic unit naapein kaise?
explanation.text: Robert Millikan ne tiny oil droplets ko electric field mein observe karke electric charge ki basic unit measure ki. 1913 ke paper se unka result famous hua.

explanation.heading: Notebooks aur excluded data
explanation.text: Rival scientist Felix Ehrenhaft smaller charges claim kar rahe the. Later historians ne Millikan ki notebooks study karke dekha ki kuch observations publication se excluded thi. Debate yeh rahi ki exclusions justified quality checks the ya publication mein unhe jis tarah describe kiya gaya woh misleading tha.

explanation.heading: Charge measure karna kyun important?
explanation.text: Atoms aur electrical devices samajhne ke liye elementary charge, yani electric charge ki basic unit, important hai. Millikan ne tiny oil droplets observe kiye. Gravity droplets ko neeche kheenchti hai; electric field charged droplets par force laga sakta hai. Motion aur forces ka analysis karke charge estimate kiya gaya.

explanation.heading: Data selection ka problem
explanation.text: Real experiments mein kuch observations unreliable ho sakti hain: droplet ka measurement disturb ho ya conditions clear na hon. Aise points exclude karna kabhi justified hota hai, par selection rules aur excluded data ke baare mein transparent reporting zaroori hai. Agar sirf favourable results dikhaye jaayen, readers uncertainty ka galat estimate laga sakte hain.

explanation.heading: Historians ka dispute
explanation.text: Millikan ki lab notebooks aur published description compare karne par historians ne kuch excluded observations identify ki. Debate is par hai ki exclusions ki quality-based reasons kitni sound thi aur publication ki language kitni transparent thi. Aaj accepted elementary charge value alag evidence se established hai. Debate ko “poori discovery fake thi” ya “sab allegations conclusively settled hain” mein reduce nahi karna chahiye.

detail.real_world_connection: Scientific results ke saath raw data aur exclusion rules clear hone se doosre researchers work evaluate kar sakte hain.

reality_check.established: Elementary charge established hai aur Millikan ki data selection par documented debate hai.
reality_check.misconception: Correct result hone se reporting ka har decision automatically correct prove nahi hota.

detail.status: Divided: the value was right; the data selection is contested

card.title: Agar mirror mein physics same chale, to universe left-right farq nahi karega?
card.hook: 1956 tak ye sirf assumption thi — kabhi test nahi hui. Pauli ne shart lagayi ki symmetry nahi tootegi. Wu ke experiment ne jawab diya: Pauli galat nikle.

detail.real_life_scene: 1956 mein do particles — theta aur tau — bilkul same lagte the: mass, charge, lifetime barabar. Par ek 2 pions mein decay karta tha, doosra 3 mein. Mirror symmetry ho to ye alag particles hone chahiye the.
detail.central_question: Kya physics ke rules mirror mein bhi waise hi chalte hain?

explanation.heading: Sawal pehle kisi ne poocha hi nahi tha
explanation.text: T.D. Lee aur C.N. Yang ne evidence dobara padha aur ek hairat-angez baat pakdi: parity conservation strong aur electromagnetic interactions mein test hui thi, par WEAK interactions mein kabhi test hi nahi hui thi. Wo ek assumption thi, ek result nahi. Unhone Phys. Rev. 104, 254 (1956) mein propose kiya ki weak interactions mein parity toot sakti hai.

explanation.heading: Pauli ko yakeen nahi tha
explanation.text: Wolfgang Pauli confident the ki symmetry tootegi nahi. Unhone January 1957 ke ek letter mein likha ki unhe nahi lagta 'Bhagwan ek kamzor left-hander hai', aur wo badi rakam ki shart lagane ko tayyar hain ki experiment symmetric result dega. Ye line physics ke sabse famous galat daav mein se ek ban gayi.

explanation.heading: Wu ne experiment kiya
explanation.text: Chien-Shiung Wu (Columbia) ne National Bureau of Standards ke Ambler, Hayward, Hoppes aur Hudson ke saath cobalt-60 nuclei ko cryogenic temperature pe magnetic field se align kiya aur beta decay ke electrons ki direction gini. Paper 15 January 1957 ko mila, 15 February ko chhapa — Phys. Rev. 105, 1413. Electrons spin ke opposite direction mein zyada nikle: parity violated.

explanation.heading: Doosri team ne dinon mein confirm kiya
explanation.text: Garwin, Lederman aur Weinrich ne muon decay wale experiment se kuch hi dinon mein wahi result confirm kiya. Theta aur tau ek hi particle nikle — aaj hum unhe kaon kehte hain. Ek 30 saal purana 'puzzle' isliye tha kyunki humne ek rule ko test kiye bina maan liya tha.

explanation.heading: Nobel gaya, par kis ko
explanation.text: 1957 ka Nobel Prize Physics mein Lee aur Yang ko mila — proposal se sirf ~13 mahine baad, jo fastest mein se ek hai. Experiment karne wali Chien-Shiung Wu ko nahi mila. Wo 1978 mein inaugural Wolf Prize jeeti aur 'First Lady of Physics' kehlayi. Ye exclusion physics ke sabse discussed credit controversies mein se ek hai.

explanation.heading: Iska matlab kya hai
explanation.text: Weak interaction mirror-symmetric nahi hai — yaani universe ke fundamental rules left aur right mein farq karte hain. Ye sirf ek curiosity nahi: isi asymmetry se matter-antimatter imbalance (CP violation) ka raasta khula, aur standard model ka structure isi pe tikka hai.

detail.real_world_connection: Aaj ka poora particle physics ka standard model chiral hai — weak force sirf left-handed particles pe lagti hai. Iska matlab: 'mirror universe' wali science-fiction idea physically alag rules wali universe hogi, sirf ulti nahi.

reality_check.established: Weak interactions parity violate karti hain — Wu et al. 1957 ne measure kiya, aur doosri teams ne confirm kiya.
reality_check.misconception: Ye sirf ek theory tha jo baad mein sahi nikla — experiment ne hi decide kiya, aur use Nobel nahi mila.

detail.status: Proven: weak interactions break mirror symmetry; Wu missed the Nobel

sources.title: Wu, Ambler, Hayward, Hoppes & Hudson 1957, Phys. Rev. 105, 1413

card.title: Agar genes apni jagah badal sakte hain, to genome stable kaise rahega?
card.hook: 1951 mein McClintock ne yahi kaha, makke ke daano ke rang se sabit karke. Hall mein na sawaal aaya na applause. 32 saal baad unhe akela Nobel mila, 81 ki umar mein.

detail.real_life_scene: Summer 1951, Cold Spring Harbor: McClintock ne maize ke results ka symposium diya. Hall mein koi sawaal nahi, koi applause nahi. Unhone baad mein likha ki unhe surprise hua — log samajh hi nahi paaye.
detail.central_question: Kya genes chromosome pe fixed hote hain, ya apni jagah badal sakte hain?

explanation.heading: Saboot makke ke daano mein tha
explanation.text: Maize (Zea mays) ke kernels ek jaise rang ke hone chahiye the, par McClintock ko aise daane mile jinpe alag-alag size aur colour ke intense patches the. Saath hi un cells mein chromosome breaks aur abnormalities bhi dikhi. Unhone microscopy aur breeding dono ka data ek saath rakha — cytology aur genetics ko jodne wali approach us waqt uncommon thi.

explanation.heading: Pehle ka explanation galat tha
explanation.text: Us variegation ko tab tak chromosome ke kuch regions ki 'zyada fragility' maana jaata tha — yaani pigment wale genes aasani se mutate ho jaate hain, aur daughter cells mein alag rang ke patches ban jaate hain. McClintock ne dikhaya ki baat mutation ki nahi, transposition ki hai: structural elements chromosome ke andar ya ek chromosome se doosre pe move kar rahe hain.

explanation.heading: 'Controlling elements'
explanation.text: Transposition se neighbouring genes inactivate ho jaate hain, isliye McClintock ne in mobile structures ko 'controlling elements' kaha. Transposition ka ek aur asar tha: jahan ye elements integrate hote the, wahan chromosome toot jaata tha. Isi system se kernel ka colour on-off hota rehta hai — ek daane pe alag-alag patches.

explanation.heading: Community ne kyun reject kiya
explanation.text: Nobel press release khud note karta hai ki ye discovery us waqt hui jab genetic code aur DNA double helix ka structure bhi pata nahi the. Us waqt gene ek fixed unit maana jaata tha — chromosome pe ek bead ki tarah. Idea ki wo khud chal phir sakte hain, genome ko unstable bana deta tha. Aur unka evidence cytological tha, jo molecular biology ki taraf ja rahi community ke liye unfamiliar tha.

explanation.heading: Proof bacteria se aaya
explanation.text: Mid-1960s mein mobile genetic elements bacteria mein demonstrate hue, aur pata chala ki wo ek bacterium se doosre mein antibiotic resistance transfer karne mein role play karte hain. Aage chalkar trypanosomes ka surface badalna (immune system se bachne ke liye) aur lymphoid cells ka seemingly infinite antibodies banana — dono isi DNA recombination pe tikke mile.

explanation.heading: 1983: akeli mahila ko unshared Nobel
explanation.text: Karolinska Institute ki Nobel Assembly ne 1983 ka Physiology or Medicine Prize Barbara McClintock ko akela diya — 'discovery of mobile genetic elements' ke liye. Press release ke mutabik ye discovery '30 saal se zyada' pehle hui thi. Wo 81 saal ki thin. Aaj pata hai ki ye elements microorganisms, insects, animals aur insaan sab mein hain, aur normal cells ko tumour cells mein badalne mein bhi transposition involved hai.

detail.real_world_connection: Transposons aaj research tools hain: gene therapy vectors, insertional mutagenesis screens, aur genome editing ke kayi methods isi 'move hone wale DNA' ki biology pe khade hain. Human genome ka ek bahut bada hissa bhi inhi se bana hai.

reality_check.established: Genes chromosome pe move kar sakte hain — McClintock ka finding confirm hua aur unhe 1983 mein unshared Nobel mila.
reality_check.misconception: Unka idea reject hua kyunki galat tha — wo reject hua kyunki tools aur framework uske liye tayyar nahi the.

detail.status: Proven: transposition documented; the Nobel came 32 years late

card.title: Agar check karna aasan hai, to dhoondhna bhi aasan hona chahiye?
card.hook: Agar ye sach nikla, to aaj ki zyada-tar encryption jis assumption pe tikki hai wahi hil jaati. 1971 se koi prove nahi kar paaya; Clay Institute ne $1M rakha hai.

detail.real_life_scene: 1971 mein Stephen Cook ne ise formal kiya, 1973 mein Leonid Levin ne USSR mein — alag-alag, ek doosre ko jaane bina. 2000 mein Clay Institute ne ise $1M ke Millennium Problems mein rakha. Jawab aaj bhi nahi.
detail.central_question: Kya efficiently check hone wali har problem efficiently solve bhi ki ja sakti hai?

explanation.heading: Problem: check karna aasan, dhoondhna mushkil — kyun?
explanation.text: Computer science mein P aur NP problems ke groups hain. Roughly, P mein kuch decision questions ko aise solve kiya ja sakta hai jinka time input size ke saath polynomial tareeke se badhta hai.

explanation.heading: 1971: Cook ne field shape di
explanation.text: NP mein proposed solution ko aise efficiently check kiya ja sakta hai. Stephen Cook ki 1971 research ne is field ko shape diya. P vs NP sawaal poochta hai: kya yeh dono groups same hain?

explanation.heading: Checking aur solving mein farq
explanation.text: Sudoku ka filled answer milne par rules check karna kabhi puzzle solve karne se easier lag sakta hai. Computer science is intuition ko precise mathematical terms mein examine karti hai. Decision problem woh question hai jiska answer yes ya no hota hai. Input size badhne par solution aur checking mein required steps ka growth compare kiya jaata hai.

explanation.heading: P aur NP simple language mein
explanation.text: P un decision problems ka class hai jinke answers polynomial-time algorithm se solve kiye ja sakte hain. Polynomial time ka rough matlab input size badhne par steps ka growth n² ya n³ jaise rule se bound ho sakta hai. NP mein yes answer ke suitable certificate ko polynomial time mein check kiya ja sakta hai. NP ka matlab “not possible” nahi.

explanation.heading: Answer important kyun hai?
explanation.text: Agar P = NP prove hota, toh many search problems ke efficient algorithms ke theoretical possibility par big consequences hote. Agar P ≠ NP prove hota, toh checking aur solving ke beech fundamental gap establish hota. Practical speed constants aur cryptography ke actual implications alag analysis maangte hain. Abhi general question unsolved hai; proof aur usable algorithm same cheez nahi.

detail.real_world_connection: Scheduling, search aur security mein difficult problems samajhne ke liye computational complexity important hai.

reality_check.established: P vs NP ek precisely defined open mathematical question hai.
reality_check.misconception: Agar P = NP prove ho bhi jaaye, usse automatically har practical password instantly toot jayega, yeh conclude nahi hota.

detail.status: Still unsolved: P vs NP, ek $1M Millennium Problem

card.title: Agar clock lekar duniya ka chakkar lagayein, to wo zameen se match karegi?
card.hook: Einstein ke mutabik nahi: chalti clock dheere chalti hai, unchai pe tez. Dono effect ulte hain. 1971 mein ye commercial flights pe test hua, aur numbers match hue.

detail.real_life_scene: October 1971: J.C. Hafele aur Richard Keating chaar caesium atomic clocks le kar Pan Am ki commercial flights pe eastward aur westward duniya ka chakkar lagaye. Predicted aur measured shifts match hue.
detail.central_question: Kya safar ki speed aur height se clock ke guzre time mein farq padta hai?

explanation.heading: Problem: chalti hui clock ka time badalta hai?
explanation.text: Einstein ki relativity ke mutabik clocks ki paths aur surroundings matter kar sakte hain. Moving clock ka elapsed time aur alag gravity level par clock ka elapsed time different ho sakta hai.

explanation.heading: 1971: clocks aircraft mein
explanation.text: 1971 mein Joseph Hafele aur Richard Keating ne atomic clocks ko commercial aircraft mein duniya ke around fly karaya aur ground reference clocks se compare kiya. Results relativity ke expected small differences ke consistent the, though actual experiment mein motion aur gravity dono effects the.

explanation.heading: Clocks compare kyun karein?
explanation.text: Hum everyday life mein assume karte hain ki har clock same rate se chalti hai. Relativity ke according elapsed time motion aur gravity ke differences se affect ho sakta hai. Effect ordinary situations mein extremely small hota hai. Precision atomic clocks in tiny differences ko measure karne ke liye useful hain.

explanation.heading: 1971 experiment
explanation.text: Joseph Hafele aur Richard Keating commercial flights par atomic clocks lekar duniya ke around gaye. Baad mein unhone clocks ko ground reference se compare kiya. Plane ki motion aur higher altitude, jahan gravity slightly different hai, dono predicted difference mein contribute karte hain. Eastward aur westward routes ke expected effects bhi same nahi hote.

explanation.heading: Technology mein fayda
explanation.text: GPS satellites par clocks aur Earth par receivers ko accurate timing chahiye, kyunki position signals ke travel time se calculate hoti hai. Relativity-related corrections include karna system design ka part hai. Plane trip par effect itna tiny hota hai ki traveller ko body mein noticeable age difference feel nahi hoga. Atomic clocks aur careful comparisons zaroori hain.

detail.real_world_connection: GPS satellites ki timing ko practical calculations mein relativity ke effects account karne padte hain.

reality_check.established: Relativistic clock differences ko experiments mein measure kiya gaya hai.
reality_check.misconception: Plane mein travel karne se insaan movie jaisa dramatically young nahi ho jaata; normal flights mein difference extremely tiny hota hai.

detail.status: Proven: predicted aur measured shift match hue

card.title: Agar hawa se roti ban sakti hai, to usi se hathiyar kyun bana?
card.hook: Haber ne 1909 mein hawa se ammonia banaya; aaj aadhi humanity ka nitrogen isi se aata hai. 1915 mein wahi aadmi Ypres pe chlorine attack direct kar raha tha.

detail.real_life_scene: 1 May 1915 ki raat, Berlin-Dahlem: Haber ki captain promotion aur Ypres 'success' ki party thi. Usi raat unki wife Clara ne garden mein khud ko army pistol se goli maar li. Agli subah Haber front ke liye nikal gaye.
detail.central_question: Kya ek discovery ko uske use se alag karke judge kiya ja sakta hai?

explanation.heading: 'Hawa se roti'
explanation.text: Haber ne 1909 mein nitrogen aur hydrogen se ammonia banane ka catalytic tareeka dikhaya — high pressure pe, catalyst ke saath. Carl Bosch ne BASF mein ise industrial scale pe banaya. Isse pehle fertilizer ka nitrogen Chile ke nitrate deposits aur guano pe depend karta tha. 1918 ka Nobel Chemistry mein Haber ko mila.

explanation.heading: Aadhi humanity isi pe tikki hai
explanation.text: Haber-Bosch process ne fertilizer ki supply ko geology se azad kar diya. Estimates ke mutabik aaj duniya ki lagbhag aadhi population ka dietary nitrogen isi process se aata hai — yaani aapke body ka nitrogen ek bade hisse mein ek 1909 ke reactor se aaya hai. Bina iske 20th century ki population growth mumkin nahi thi.

explanation.heading: Aur wahi cheez weapon ban gayi
explanation.text: Ammonia se explosives bhi bante hain. Jab war shuru hui to nitrogen supply ka matlab tha munitions supply. 22 April 1915 ko Ypres pe ~168 tonnes chlorine gas cylinders se chhodi gayi — attack Haber ki direction mein hua. Wo Berlin wapas hero ki tarah laute, aur captain bana diye gaye.

explanation.heading: Clara ka apna career khatm ho chuka tha
explanation.text: Clara Immerwahr 1900 mein University of Breslau se doctorate paane wali pehli mahila bani. 1901 mein Haber se shaadi hui. Female scientists ke liye koi employment nahi thi, isliye wo women ki continuing education mein freelance instructing karti rahin — zyadatar housewives ko padhati thin. 23 April 1909 ko unhone apne PhD adviser Richard Abegg ko likha: 'Jo Fritz ne pichhle aath saalon mein paaya hai, maine wo khoya hai, aur jo mujhme bacha hai wo mujhe gehri asantushti se bharta hai.'

explanation.heading: Motivation pe asli jhagda
explanation.text: Popular version kehti hai Clara ne gas warfare ko 'science ke ideals ka perversion' kaha aur protest mein jaan di. Par Friedrich aur Hoffmann ke 2016 scholarly review ko iske liye 'little evidence' mila; unke mutabik ye pacifist-martyr framing 1990s mein popular hui — 'the myth of Clara Immerwahr'. Jo documented hai: maut us raat hui, umar 45 thi, pistol Haber ki thi, aur Haber agle din front chale gaye.

explanation.heading: Haber ka apna ant bhi isi kahani ka hissa hai
explanation.text: Haber Jewish family mein paida hue the aur Christianity mein convert hue the. 1933 mein Nazi rules ke under unhe apne Jewish colleagues ko nikaalna pada; unhone protest mein resignation diya aur Germany chhod diya. January 1934 mein Basel mein exile ke dauraan unki maut hui — us desh se door jiske liye unhone gas warfare direct kiya tha.

detail.real_world_connection: Haber ka naam toxicology mein aaj bhi zinda hai: 'Haber's rule' kehti hai ki effect = concentration × time. Aur ek hi discovery ka dohra use — khana aur hathiyar — aaj bhi AI, nuclear aur gene editing ke ethics debates ka central example hai.

reality_check.established: Haber-Bosch process documented hai aur duniya ki food supply ka base hai; Ypres attack mein Haber ki bhumika bhi documented hai.
reality_check.misconception: Clara ne gas warfare ke protest mein suicide kiya — 2016 scholarly review ke mutabik is motive ka little evidence hai.

detail.status: Divided: the chemistry is settled; Clara's motive is disputed
